chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad ibn Uthman from Al-Halabi said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about fish that are found floating on the water or that the sea casts up dead, so he said: Do not eat it.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating fish that die naturally in the water and float to the surface?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) prohibits consuming fish that die in the water (floating or washed ashore), distinguishing them from fish caught while alive. This ruling is central to Shia jurisprudence, where the death of fish in water is considered a form of *maytah* (unclean carcass), contrasting with the Sunni view that all sea creatures are permissible. The chain of transmission highlights the reliability of early scholars like Hammad ibn Uthman in preserving this specific legal distinction.
